## **Why Multivariate Normal Distributions?**

## **The Experimental Strategy**

We systematically vary:

- dimensionality,
- variance structure,
- correlation structure,
- anisotropy,
- coordinate representation.

The main quantities of interest are:

- warmup length,
- nested $\widehat{R}$,
- mean squared error.

## **1. Bivariate Normal Distributions**

### Bivariate covariance structures

Select the two variables to display their corresponding covariance plot.

```{=html}
<div class="bivariate-controls">
  <button onclick="showBivariatePlot(1, 1)">1–1</button>
  <button onclick="showBivariatePlot(10, 10)">10–10</button>
  <button onclick="showBivariatePlot(100, 100)">100–100</button>
  <button onclick="showBivariatePlot(1000, 1000)">1000–1000</button>
  <button onclick="showBivariatePlot(10, 1)">10–1</button>
  <button onclick="showBivariatePlot(100, 1)">100–1</button>
  <button onclick="showBivariatePlot(100, 10)">100–10</button>
  <button onclick="showBivariatePlot(1000, 1)">1000–1</button>
  <button onclick="showBivariatePlot(1000, 10)">1000–10</button>
  <button onclick="showBivariatePlot(1000, 100)">1000–100</button>
</div>

<div class="bivariate-plot-panel">
  <img
    id="bivariate-plot"
    src="figures/chapter05/cov1_1.png"
    alt="Bivariate covariance plot for 1 and 1"
  >
</div>

<script>
(function () {
  const BASE = "figures/chapter05/";

  const plot = document.getElementById("bivariate-plot");

  plot.addEventListener("error", function () {
    plot.classList.add("error");
    plot.alt = "MISSING: " + plot.getAttribute("src");
  });

  plot.addEventListener("load", function () {
    plot.classList.remove("error");
  });

  window.showBivariatePlot = function (var1, var2) {
    plot.src = BASE + "cov" + var1 + "_" + var2 + ".png";
    plot.alt = "Bivariate covariance plot for " + var1 + " and " + var2;
  };
})();
</script>
```
